receivedItems.description: Hye-Jin Choi overcame difficult scoring conditions to shoot a 2-over 74 but still maintained a two-stroke lead after two rounds of the LPGA Shanghai tournament.

receivedItems.headline: Hye-Jin Choi takes 1st-round lead at Shanghai LPGA event
receivedItems.description: Hye-Jin Choi shot an 8-under 64 to take a three-stroke lead after the first round of the Shanghai event.

receivedItems.headline: LPGA's '27 schedule features higher purses, better travel efficiency
receivedItems.description: The LPGA Tour 2027 schedule will feature 33 tournaments, a record $147 million in prize money and a more efficient travel itinerary for its players.

receivedItems.headline: Jeeno Thitikul wins in Hawaii for her 4th LPGA Tour victory of the season
receivedItems.description: Jeeno Thitikul of Thailand quickly overcame a late double bogey to win the LOTTE Championship for her fourth LPGA Tour victory of the season.

receivedItems.headline: Jeeno Thitikul, Polly Mack birdie 18th for share of lead in Honolulu
receivedItems.description: Second-ranked Jeeno Thitikul of Thailand made a 12-foot birdie putt on the par-5 18th for a 7-under 65 a share of the second-round lead Friday in the LPGA Tour's LOTTE Championship.

receivedItems.headline: A Lim Kim fires 65 at rainy Hoakalei to take lead in LOTTE Championship
receivedItems.description: A Lim Kim shot a 7-under 65 on a rainy and breezy Thursday at Hoakalei to take the first-round lead in the LPGA Tour's LOTTE Championship.

receivedItems.headline: Butch Harmon, Dottie Pepper among Hall of Fame finalists
receivedItems.description: Butch Harmon and Dottie Pepper, who came close to induction two years ago, are among the 14 finalists for the 2027 World Golf Hall of Fame induction class.

images.name: Golf HOF 141216 [600x400]
images.alt: World Golf Hall of Fame

receivedItems.headline: Japan's Yuna Nishimura wins LPGA Tour's Walmart NW Arkansas
receivedItems.description: Yuna Nishimura played a flawless back nine after allowing the chasing pack to get close early and won the Walmart NW Arkansas Championship by five shots on Sunday for her first LPGA victory.

images.name: Yuna Nishimura [600x600]
images.caption: Yuna Nishimura celebrates after winning the Walmart NW Arkansas Championship on Sunday.

receivedItems.headline: Coughlin first in LPGA history to open round with 9 straight birdies
receivedItems.description: Lauren Coughlin made LPGA history when she birdied her first nine holes at the Walmart NW Arkansas Championship on Saturday.

images.name: Lauren Coughlin [600x400]
images.caption: Lauren Coughlin's nine straight birdies keyed a second-round 61 on Saturday, moving her up 106 spots on the leaderboard into a tie for 21st.

receivedItems.headline: Team Europe reclaims Solheim Cup with Sunday splash over U.S.
receivedItems.description: The Solheim Cup is back in the hands of the Europeans after Lottie Woad holed a putt from 2 feet on No. 17 to guarantee Team Europe would reach the 14½ points needed to beat the United States.

receivedItems.headline: Jennifer Kupcho sinks unlikely putts to even Solheim Cup
receivedItems.description: Jennifer Kupcho rolled in two late birdie putts -- one from 93 feet -- to earn the Americans an unlikely point and tie the Solheim Cup at 8-8 after four sessions.

images.name: 260912 jennifer kupcho photo [1296x729]
images.caption: Jennifer Kupcho celebrates after sinking a second straight long putt to win her match and even the Solheim Cup.

receivedItems.headline: Europe builds 7-5 lead at Solheim Cup after Korda, Corpuz falter
receivedItems.description: Team Europe finally took down the record-setting U.S. partnership of Nelly Korda and Allisen Corpuz at the Solheim Cup on the way to winning the morning foursomes and building a 7-5 lead after three sessions.

receivedItems.headline: Solheim Cup: Europe, U.S. tied 4-4 after Ciganda's late heroics
receivedItems.description: Europe's Carlota Ciganda pulled off an unlikely par after Americans Nelly Korda and Lauren Coughlin left birdie putts short to gain a half-point with rookie Julia Lopez Ramirez and leave the teams tied at 4-4 after Day 1 at the Solheim Cup.

receivedItems.headline: Europe, U.S. tied at 2-2 after opening session of Solheim Cup
receivedItems.description: Nelly Korda played like the world No. 1 in a record-setting partnership with Allisen Corpuz, helping the Americans split the opening foursomes 2-2 with Team Europe in a loud and wet start to the Solheim Cup.

receivedItems.headline: Solheim Cup to begin with Nelly Korda-Charley Hull matchup
receivedItems.description: Europe's top two players, Charley Hull and Lottie Woad, will open the Solheim Cup against a U.S. pairing containing top-ranked Nelly Korda.

images.name: Nelly Korda [600x400]
images.caption: Nelly Korda hits her drive on the first hole of the final round of the U.S. Women's Open.
images.alt: Nelly Korda

receivedItems.headline: Ruoning Yin birdies 18 to take the 1-shot lead at TPC Boston
receivedItems.description: Ruoning Yin chipped in for birdie from just off the 18th green to take the third-round lead Saturday at TPC Boston in the FM Championship.

receivedItems.headline: Miyu Yamashita keeps rolling, shares 2nd-round lead at FM Championship
receivedItems.description: Miyu Yamashita was back on top of an LPGA Tour leaderboard days after tying the tour's 72-hole scoring record in a nine-stroke victory in Canada.

images.name: 260820 Yamashita [600x400]
images.caption: Miyu Yamashita ended her Thursday morning round at Royal Mayfair atop the leaderboard -- despite the abundance of mosquitoes on the course.

receivedItems.headline: Sei Young Kim shoots 64 for 1st-round lead in FM Championship
receivedItems.description: Sei Young Kim capped a second-nine spree with a chip-in eagle and shot an 8-under 64 on Thursday at the TPC Boston to take the first-round lead in the FM Championship.

receivedItems.headline: LPGA Tour announces plans for Hong Kong event next year
receivedItems.description: The LPGA Tour and presenting sponsor Moomoo announced plans Wednesday for an event in Hong Kong beginning next year.

receivedItems.headline: 3-time major champ, Solheim captain Anna Nordqvist retiring
receivedItems.description: Three-time major champion Anna Nordqvist will retire as a player after this weekend's FM Championship in Boston, saying she will pivot to focus on her health and family.

receivedItems.headline: Miyu Yamashita matches LPGA Tour 72-hole scoring record in CPKC win
receivedItems.description: Japanese star Miyu Yamashita matched the LPGA Tour's 72-hole scoring record Sunday in a wire-to-wire, nine-stroke victory in the CPKC Women's Open at Royal Mayfair.

receivedItems.headline: Yamashita's CPKC Women's Open lead up to 6 shots after 65
receivedItems.description: Miyu Yamashita will bid for a wire-to-wire victory after stretching her lead in the CPKC Women's Open to six shots following a 5-under 65 on Saturday.

receivedItems.headline: Yamashita widens CPKC Women's Open lead to 5 shots after 64
receivedItems.description: After an opening-round 62, Miyu Yamashita shot 64 on Friday afternoon to open a five-shot lead in the CPKC Women's Open.

images.name: Miyu Yamashita [600x400]
images.credit: Darryl Dyck/The Canadian Press via AP

receivedItems.headline: Miyu Yamashita opens with 62 to lead CPKC Women's Open
receivedItems.description: Miyu Yamashita shot an 8-under 62 on Thursday for a one-stroke lead over fellow Japanese player Nasa Hataoka in the CPKC Women's Open, with two Canadian teenagers on the leaderboard in the national championship.

images.name: 260820 Yamashita [600x400]
images.caption: Miyu Yamashita ended her Thursday morning round at Royal Mayfair atop the leaderboard -- despite the abundance of mosquitoes on the course.

receivedItems.headline: Jeeno Thitikul rallies with final-round 64 to win in Portland
receivedItems.description: Jeeno Thitikul ran off five straight birdies early and closed with an 8-under 64 for a one-shot victory Sunday in The Standard Portland Classic, her third LPGA Tour title of the season.

images.name: Jeeno Thitikul LPGA Portland_260816 [1296x729]
images.caption: Jeeno Thitikul won the The Standard Portland Classic on Sunday for her third LPGA Tour victory of the season.
images.alt: Jeeno Thitikul won the The Standard Portland Classic on Sunday for her third LPGA Tour victory of the season.

receivedItems.headline: Sophia Schubert, Arpichaya Yubol share 2-shot lead in Portland
receivedItems.description: Sophia Schubert birdied two of the final three holes for a 5-under 67 and a share of the lead with Arpichaya Yubol on Saturday in The Standard Portland Classic.

receivedItems.headline: Arpichaya Yubol takes LPGA Tour lead into weekend in Portland
receivedItems.description: Arpichaya Yubol shot her second straight 6-under 66 to take the second-round lead in The Standard Portland Classic.

receivedItems.headline: Mariel Galdiano leads Portland Classic by 1 shot
receivedItems.description: Mariel Galdiano posted a 7-under 65 in one of the first groups Thursday in The Standard Portland Classic, and watched it hold up for a one-stroke lead.

receivedItems.headline: Inkster Award-winner Megha Ganne to make LPGA debut in Portland
receivedItems.description: Megha Ganne makes her LPGA debut as a pro this week at The Standard Portland Classic with an exemption from winning the Inkster Award.

images.name: 260811 Ganne [1296x729]
images.caption: Megha Ganne, a four-time All-America at Stanford who won the U.S. Women's Amateur, will make her LPGA debut at The Standard Portland Classic this week.

receivedItems.headline: Asterisk Talley wins U.S. Women's Amateur for 2nd USGA title
receivedItems.description: Asterisk Talley picked up her biggest win yet Sunday when she surged past Anna Iwanaga of Japan for an 8-and-6 victory to win the U.S. Women's Amateur.

images.name: Asterisk Talley [600x600]
images.caption: Asterisk Talley led 3 up after the opening 18, then poured it on in the afternoon to close out her match against Anna Iwanaga on the 12th hole.

receivedItems.headline: Corning Classic returns to LPGA schedule featuring $5M payout
receivedItems.description: The Corning Classic is returning to the LPGA Tour schedule in 2027 after an 18-year absence, offering a $5 million purse that ranks among the richest outside the majors.

receivedItems.headline: Team Europe adds Maguire, 3 rookies to Solheim Cup team
receivedItems.description: Europe captain Anna Nordqvist finalized her Solheim Cup team Monday by adding veteran Leona Maguire and three rookies as her picks for the Sept. 11-13 matches in The Netherlands.

receivedItems.headline: ATP Finals preview: Can Alcaraz close out the year with a big win?
receivedItems.description: Alcaraz has returned from injury and is on a hot streak, while Americans Shelton and Tiafoe are hoping to challenge for the ATP Finals title.

images.name: Carlos Alcaraz [1296x729]
images.caption: Carlos Alcaraz won the Paris Masters on Sunday, and the Vienna Open the week before.

images.caption: Novak Djokovic missed out on qualifying for the ATP Finals, in what would have been a record-setting 19th appearance.

images.caption: Alexander Zverev won two major titles this season, and Ben Shelton made his first major final appearance.

images.name: Jodar celeb Madrid Open_260422 [1296x729] - Copy
images.caption: Rafael Jodar began 2026 ranked No. 168 in the world -- and is now ranked No. 9.

receivedItems.headline: Waiting game pays off for Tiafoe as he heads into ATP Finals
receivedItems.description: At 28, Frances Tiafoe has played in just about every tournament on tour. But this will be his first experience in the ATP Finals.

images.name: Frances Tiafoe ATP Finals [1296x729]
images.caption: Frances Tiafoe will play in his first ATP Finals, beginning on Sunday in Turin, Italy.

images.name: Ben Shelton and Frances Tiafoe [1296x729] - Copy
images.caption: Tiafoe made it to the US Open semifinals in September, before losing to Ben Shelton.

receivedItems.headline: Jannik Sinner (knee) plans return at Saudi exhibition in Aussie prep
receivedItems.description: Jannik Sinner, who has not played since July with a knee injury, said Tuesday he aims to return at an exhibition in Saudi Arabia in late December.

receivedItems.headline: Carlos Alcaraz beats Ben Shelton to win Paris Masters title
receivedItems.description: Carlos Alcaraz won his second straight title and fifth of the year with a straight-sets victory over Ben Shelton in the Paris Masters final.

images.name: Carlos Alcaraz [1296x729]
images.alt: Carlos Alcaraz

receivedItems.headline: Carlos Alcaraz looking for 'revenge' against Ben Shelton in Paris Masters final
receivedItems.description: Carlos Alcaraz reached his third final since the US Open when he beat Casper Ruud 6-4, 6-4 at the Paris Masters. Alcaraz will play Ben Shelton for the title.

images.name: Shelton Alcaraz feature lede [600x400]
images.caption: Ben Shelton defeated Carlos Alcaraz in the US Open quarterfinals -- becoming the first American to defeat Alcaraz at a major.

receivedItems.headline: Gaël Monfils stays in tennis as captain of France's Davis Cup team
receivedItems.description: Gaël Monfils will stay in tennis as captain of France's Davis Cup team, the national federation said.

receivedItems.headline: Alcaraz, Shelton into Paris Masters semis; ATP Finals field set
receivedItems.description: Carlos Alcaraz held off Taylor Fritz and Ben Shelton outlasted Tommy Paul to reach the Paris Masters semifinals while also finalizing the field for the ATP Finals.

receivedItems.headline: Ben Shelton tops Tommy Paul to reach first Paris Masters semifinal
receivedItems.description: Ben Shelton won an all-American matchup against Tommy Paul on Friday to reach the semifinals of the Paris Masters for the first time.

receivedItems.headline: Jannik Sinner replacing Darren Cahill with Magnus Norman on coaching team
receivedItems.description: Jannik Sinner's partnership with coach Darren Cahill is ending after a spell that saw the Italian win five Grand Slam titles and achieve the No. 1 ranking.

images.name: Jannik Sinner of Italy celebrates with his coach Darren Cahill  [600x400]

receivedItems.headline: Ben Shelton moves into Paris Masters quarters, to face Tommy Paul next
receivedItems.description: Ben Shelton beat Arthur Rinderknech 3-6, 6-4, 7-6 (5) on Thursday for a season's best 43rd win and a spot in the Paris Masters quarterfinals. The US Open runner-up next faces No. 12 Tommy Paul in an all-American contest.

images.name: Ben Shelton [600x400]
images.credit: Photo by Mustafa Yalcin/Anadolu via Getty Images

receivedItems.headline: Alexander Zverev loses first match as No. 1; Novak Djokovic also out in Paris
receivedItems.description: Alexander Zverev's tenure as the No. 1 player in men's tennis started with a 7-6 (5), 6-2 defeat to Lorenzo Musetti, while Novak Djokovic saw his dwindling hopes of making the ATP Finals with a loss to qualifier Rinky Hijikata.

images.name: Alexander Zverev [1296x729] - Copy
images.caption: Alexander Zverev became world No. 1 on Monday.

receivedItems.headline: Novak Djokovic fends off Valentin Vacherot at Paris Masters
receivedItems.description: Seven-time champion Novak Djokovic overcame a scare late in the second set to beat big-serving Valentin Vacherot in the first round of the Paris Masters.

receivedItems.headline: FAQ: Why Zverev's rise to world No. 1 provokes mixed feelings
receivedItems.description: Alexander Zverev's climb to No. 1 presents a complicated scenario for fans, sponsors and media due to his history of domestic violence allegations.

images.name: Alexander Zverev [1296x729] - Copy
images.caption: Alexander Zverev became world No. 1 on Monday.

images.name: Zverev Shelton feature lede [1296x729] - Copy
images.caption: Zverev defeated Ben Shelton in the US Open final in September.

images.name: Zverev Sinner [1296x729] - Copy
images.caption: Zverev is not likely to remain No. 1 long, as Jannik Sinner (pictured) and Carlos Alcaraz return to full health.

images.name: Alexander Zverev French Open [1296x729] - Copy
images.caption: Zverev won the first major title of his career at the French Open in June.

receivedItems.headline: Alexander Zverev rises to No. 1 men's tennis ranking after dominant season
receivedItems.description: Alexander Zverev rose to No. 1 in the men's tennis ranking after a dominant season in which he won the French and US Open titles.

images.name: Alexander Zverev French Open [1296x729] - Copy (2) 20261102
images.caption: Zverev won the first major title of his career at the French Open in June.

receivedItems.headline: Ben Shelton adds coach Juan Carlos Ferrero to 2027 staff
receivedItems.description: Carlos Alcaraz's former coach Juan Carlos Ferrero is joining Ben Shelton's coaching staff for the 2027 season.

receivedItems.headline: Valentin Vacherot rallies to beat Jiri Lehecka to win Swiss Indoors title
receivedItems.description: Valentin Vacherot clinched his second career title after beating Jiri Lehecka 2-6, 6-3, 6-3 in the Swiss Indoors final.

receivedItems.headline: Carlos Alcaraz beats Alex de Minaur to win Vienna Open for fourth title of 2026
receivedItems.description: Carlos Alcaraz beat Alex de Minaur 6-1, 6-4 to win the Vienna Open and defeat his opponent for the seventh time in as many meetings.

receivedItems.headline: Novak Djokovic loses to Jan-Lennard Struff at Swiss Indoors
receivedItems.description: Novak Djokovic had a tough loss Thursday at the Swiss Indoors, going down 6-7 (4), 7-5, 7-6 (5) to 47th-ranked Jan-Lennard Struff. He remains one career title behind Roger Federer's 103.

receivedItems.headline: Alexander Zverev's first No. 1 ranking to be confirmed Monday with win in Vienna
receivedItems.description: Alexander Zverev will finally rise to be the No. 1 men's tennis player Monday when the next rankings are published.

receivedItems.headline: Stan Wawrinka retires as Basel farewell ends in 1st-round loss
receivedItems.description: Stan Wawrinka's illustrious tennis career finally came to an end on Tuesday at his home tournament in Basel.

receivedItems.headline: Retired Rafael Nadal to play in Las Vegas exhibition in February
receivedItems.description: Rafael Nadal, winner of 22 Grand Slam titles, will play in a tennis exhibition in Las Vegas early next year, his first time playing in the U.S. since retiring two years ago.

images.name: Rafael Nadal [600x400]
images.caption: Five-time champion Rafael Nadal lost in the Round of 16 at the Madrid Open.

receivedItems.headline: Davidovich Fokina upsets Zverev, faces Jodar for Shanghai title
receivedItems.description: Alejandro Davidovich Fokina upset future No. 1 Alexander Zverev 5-7, 6-4, 6-3 to reach the Shanghai Masters final, where he will face 20-year-old Rafael Jodar.

receivedItems.headline: Rafael Jodar makes Shanghai Masters history, sets up semifinal vs. Medvedev
receivedItems.description: Rafael Jodar, 20, became the youngest semifinalist in Shanghai Masters history and will next meet Daniil Medvedev.

receivedItems.headline: Proposed ATP Tour changes address player welfare, compensation
receivedItems.description: The ATP Tour is proposing several rule changes in an effort to address player welfare, additional compensation, and enhancing pension and retirement benefits.

receivedItems.headline: Alexander Zverev wins in straight sets to reach Shanghai Masters semifinals
receivedItems.description: Top-ranked Alexander Zverev said he felt good on-court after beating Alex de Minaur 6-4, 6-4 at the Shanghai Masters.

receivedItems.headline: Drug-testing agency lists Monfils as retired, seemingly ruling out Paris farewell
receivedItems.description: French tennis player Gael Monfils has entered retirement, a move that came a bit earlier than what was expected.

receivedItems.headline: Medvedev beats longtime rival Tsitsipas, reaches Shanghai Masters quarterfinals
receivedItems.description: Daniil Medvedev is back in the Shanghai Masters quarterfinals after getting the better of Stefanos Tsitsipas in the latest chapter of their longtime rivalry.

receivedItems.headline: Zverev beats Bublik to reach Shanghai Masters quarters
receivedItems.description: Alexander Zverev beat Alexander Bublik 7-6 (6), 4-6, 7-6 (1) to reach the Shanghai Masters quarterfinals on Tuesday in his first match since securing the year-end No. 1 ranking.

receivedItems.headline: Zverev snags No. 1 ranking with Alcaraz loss, Sinner injury
receivedItems.description: Alexander Zverev, 29, who won his first two Grand Slam titles this year, has clinched the year-end No. 1 men's tennis ranking.

images.name: Alexander Zverev captures first US Open title of his career
images.caption: Alexander Zverev captures first US Open title of his career

receivedItems.headline: Zizou Bergs stuns Carlos Alcaraz in straight sets in Shanghai
receivedItems.description: Zizou Bergs stunned second-seeded Carlos Alcaraz 7-5, 7-6 (4) on Monday to advance to the fourth round of the Shanghai Masters.

receivedItems.headline: Ben Shelton stumbles in straight sets, Zverev wins in Shanghai
receivedItems.description: Ben Shelton lost 7-6 (5), 7-6 (3) to 21-year-old Frenchman Arthur Gea in the third round of the Shanghai Masters, while Alexander Zverev continued his push for the No. 1 ranking with a win.

receivedItems.headline: Carlos Alcaraz tests new mustache in opening Shanghai win
receivedItems.description: Carlos Alcaraz sported a mustache along with his team in the stands as he swept to a 6-3, 6-3 victory over Juan Manuel Cerundolo at the Shanghai Masters.

images.name: 261010 alcaraz photo [1296x729]
images.caption: Carlos Alcaraz said the mustache was a result of his title victory at the Japan Open.

receivedItems.headline: Novak Djokovic beaten by Hubert Hurkacz at Shanghai Masters
receivedItems.description: Novak Djokovic was knocked out of the Shanghai Masters after a shock second-round loss to Hubert Hurkacz on Friday.

receivedItems.headline: Shelton breezes to straight-sets win to advance in Shanghai
receivedItems.description: On his 24th birthday, Ben Shelton defeated Daniel Altmaier 6-3, 7-6 (6) to advance to the third round of the Shanghai Masters.

receivedItems.headline: Djokovic to reach out to Sinner about returning from long layoff
receivedItems.description: Novak Djokovic plans to reach out to Jannik Sinner after an injury ended the top-ranked player's season, saying Thursday he knows how difficult it is to come back after a lengthy layoff.

images.name: Djokovic and Sinner preview lede [600x400]
images.caption: Jannik Sinner, 24, will take on Novak Djokovic, 39, on Friday at Wimbledon.

receivedItems.headline: Alcaraz: Tennis schedule is pushing players too hard
receivedItems.description: Alcaraz: Tennis schedule is pushing players too hard

images.name: Alcaraz: Tennis schedule is pushing players too hard
images.caption: Alcaraz: Tennis schedule is pushing players too hard

receivedItems.headline: Tsitsipas advances in Shanghai; Hurkacz lines up Djokovic
receivedItems.description: Two-time major finalist Stefanos Tsitsipas beat Kimmer Coppejans in the Shanghai Masters first round to continue his slow climb back up the ATP rankings, while Hubert Hurkacz had 19 aces in a win over James Duckworth and next plays Novak Djokovic.

receivedItems.headline: Djokovic wins 7th China Open title after injured De Minaur retires
receivedItems.description: Novak Djokovic won his 7th China Open title Tuesday after Alex de Minaur retired in the second set of the final with a groin injury.

receivedItems.headline: Carlos Alcaraz retains Japan Open title in big step following injury layoff
receivedItems.description: Third-ranked Carlos Alcaraz beat Jiri Lehecka on Tuesday to defend his Japan Open title, in his second tournament back from an injury layoff.

receivedItems.headline: Jannik Sinner to miss rest of year due to knee inflammation
receivedItems.description: Jannik Sinner, who already announced he'd miss the Shanghai Masters, announced Tuesday he would miss the rest of the year due to knee inflammation.

receivedItems.headline: Medvedev out of China Open after smashing ball in fan's face
receivedItems.description: Daniil Medvedev was disqualified from his semifinal China Open match against Novak Djokovic after hitting a ball into the stands and striking a fan in the head. Djokovic advances to the final Tuesday vs. Alex de Minaur.

images.name: Daniil Medvedev DQ'd after hitting ball into stands that strikes spectator's face
images.caption: Daniil Medvedev DQ'd after hitting ball into stands that strikes spectator's face

receivedItems.headline: No. 3 Alcaraz overcomes big deficit to reach Japan Open final
receivedItems.description: No. 3-ranked Carlos Alcaraz overcame losing 16 straight points to beat Jaume Munar 5-7, 6-3, 6-1 to make the Japan Open final. It will be Alcaraz's first final since coming back from a 4 1/2-month layoff for a wrist injury.

images.name: Carlos Alcaraz [1296x729]
images.caption: 2026 Japan Open semis

receivedItems.headline: Carlos Alcaraz advances to Tokyo semis after Shapovalov injury
receivedItems.description: Carlos Alcaraz moved into the final four at the Tokyo Open after his quarterfinal opponent, Denis Shapovalov, was forced to retire due to a hip injury.

receivedItems.headline: Sinner extends absence by withdrawing from Shanghai Masters
receivedItems.description: Top-ranked Jannik Sinner has withdrawn from the Shanghai Masters as he deals with a knee problem.

images.name: Jannik Sinner of Italy plays a backhand against Alexander Zverev of Germany during their Gentlemen's Singles final match photodesk [600x400]

receivedItems.headline: Alcaraz beats Arnaldi to reach 3rd round at Japan Open

requestPayload.instructions:
You are the final editor for Sports Big Board Sports Ticker.

You are NOT a researcher. You have NO browsing task. Use ONLY the candidate packet
provided by Python. Never add a fact that is not supported by one or more cited
candidateIds.

Goal: create a concise rolling "what actually happened or materially changed in
the last 24 hours?" ticker. This is NOT an article feed.

HARD NEWS TEST
For every selected item, you must be able to answer:
"What happened or changed?"
Do NOT select an item merely because ESPN published analysis, opinion, a feature,
a prediction, a preview, a quote, a question article, or a discussion topic.

Selection priorities:
1. BREAKING / major league news
2. playoff and standings consequences
3. major injuries / returns
4. trades / signings / contracts
5. records / milestones / record chases
6. rankings / awards / streaks / slumps
7. discipline / legal / actual coaching personnel changes / meaningful roster/depth-chart changes
8. major upsets
9. meaningful results
10. weak previews only when a genuinely NEW development makes them ticker-worthy

PRIORITY SCALE — ALWAYS USE THE FULL 1-100 SCALE
Priority is importance, NOT rank number.
- 95-100: extraordinary / sport-dominating breaking development
- 88-94: major national story, major playoff/championship consequence, blockbuster transaction
- 80-87: highly important injury, signing, record, upset, legal/discipline or standings development
- 70-79: strong league-wide story, notable return/milestone/ranking change
- 70-79: strong grounded result story: standout performance, late winner, milestone,
  meaningful first/clinching win, or similarly useful game context
- 60-69: useful normal ticker item; a close score alone belongs here, not in the 70s
- 50-65: ordinary completed result unless supplied metadata proves major context
- below 50: usually omit unless the league has exceptionally little legitimate news
Never use 1, 2, 3... as ranking positions. rank is assigned later by Python.

TYPE RULES
- COACHING means a coaching personnel/status change: hired, fired, resigned,
  extended, promoted, demoted, or role changed. A coach giving a quote is NOT COACHING.
- RESULT means a completed game/match result.
- UPSET means the supplied candidate establishes a genuinely surprising result.
- RETURN means a player actually returned/was activated after absence.
- DEPTH_CHART means a starter/backup/role change, not merely unavailable players.
- OTHER should be rare.
- For structured RESULT candidates, use metadata such as homeTeam, awayTeam,
  scores, ranks, FBS context, fusedContext, and resultEnrichment. Do not invent
  context that is not present in the candidate.
- If metadata.resultEnrichment.decisiveMoment exists, the headline and detail
  MUST lead with that decisive moment rather than merely restating the final score.
- Treat metadata.resultEnrichment.headlineSeed and summarySeed as grounded
  editorial seeds. You may tighten their wording, but do not remove the decisive
  fact they contain.
- metadata.storyPromotion is Python's strongest grounded result-story context.
  If storyPromotion exists, prefer its headlineSeed/summarySeed over a generic
  "Team A beat Team B" score headline. The headline should teach the reader WHY
  the result mattered or HOW it happened.
- When choosing among ordinary RESULT candidates, prefer higher storyPromotion.storyScore.
  A decisive-moment promotion or standout performance should beat a generic close
  score with no known story.
- Never use raw evidence boilerplate such as "Highlightly final:" as user-facing
  ticker copy when storyPromotion or fusedContext provides richer grounded prose.
- Never say walk-off, blocked kick, last-second, buzzer-beater, overtime,
  game-winner, or comeback unless those facts are present in resultEnrichment
  or another grounded candidate source.

Editorial mix rules:
- A RESULT should have a reason to exist: decisive finish, standout performance,
  upset, ranked consequence, playoff/standings consequence, milestone, comeback,
  or another grounded story hook. Prefer omission over padding.
- A generic draw or routine score with no story hook is low value and should
  normally be omitted.
- Maximum 5 ordinary RESULT items per base league.
- Maximum 2 combined NEXT/SCHEDULE items per base league.
- Do not pad a league.
- A major UPSET is not an ordinary RESULT.
- Special Events should cover important active events outside the seven base leagues.
- A Special Event name must be grounded in the selected candidate itself. Never place
  a Monaco Grand Prix story under the Italian Grand Prix merely because the Italian
  Grand Prix is the currently active F1 weekend. If the candidate names a specific
  tournament/race/event, use that event name.

Grounding:
- Every final item must reference candidateIds from the supplied packet.
- Do not invent URLs, scores, dates, injuries, rankings, records, quotes, or transactions.
- If Python has already fused multiple sources into one candidate, treat that
  candidate's fusedContext metadata as grounded support for that same candidateId.
- If a candidate is ambiguous, omit it rather than guessing.

FRESHNESS BASIS
freshnessBasis must be a concrete factual clause describing the new development.
GOOD: "Chicago activated Kyle Teel from the injured list Friday."
GOOD: "Sacramento agreed to a one-year deal with Ben Simmons Friday."
GOOD: "Liverpool beat Ipswich 2-0 for its first league win of the season."
BAD: "hours ago"
BAD: "today"
BAD: "recently"
BAD: "new report"
Never return a vague time phrase by itself.

Consistency:
- Do not say shutout/shut out/blanked if the opponent scored.
- Do not call something a one-point win unless the score margin is one.
- Do not call a routine result an upset without evidence in the candidate packet.

OUTPUT SHAPE
The "leagues" field is an object with EXACTLY these seven required keys:
MLB, NFL, NBA, NHL, EPL, MLS, NCAAF.
Each key contains only "items". Python owns season-state determination.
Do not rename, duplicate, or omit league keys.

Write factual, compact, non-clickbait ticker copy.


A4 GLOBAL FEED BUDGET — CRITICAL
The finished Sports Ticker is ONE continuously scrolling feed across every base
league and every Special Event. The headline budget is GLOBAL, never per league.

- Preferred final total: 30-35 headlines across EVERYTHING combined.
- Editorial target before Python's final safety/diversity pass: 32-35 headlines.
- 35 is a hard ceiling for the final feed, not a target for each section.
- Never pad with analysis, generic previews, weak rumors, or meaningless scores
  just to reach 30. If fewer than 30 genuinely useful stories exist, return fewer.
- Conversely, do not stop at 2-3 items per league when several legitimate fresh
  stories exist and the combined feed is still below target.
- Think like a national sports-news desk building one ribbon, not seven separate
  league newsletters.

GLOBAL MIX
- Major breaking news, playoffs, records, major injuries, transactions, upsets,
  standings/rank changes, and decisive result stories should beat routine scores.
- Active/postseason leagues with a legitimate fresh development should usually be
  represented, but there is no hard quota for any league.
- Avoid allowing one league or one story type to dominate simply because it has
  many similar results. Six to eight strong items from one active league can be fine
  when the overall news day supports it; a wall of routine scores is not.
- Special Events compete directly with base-league stories for the same 30-35
  global slots.

HEADLINE LENGTH — CRITICAL FOR THE ON-SCREEN RIBBON
- Headlines are display copy, not article titles. Aim for 45-64 characters.
- HARD maximum: 72 characters, including spaces and punctuation.
- Keep the key actor + development/result; move secondary context into the text field.
- Prefer compact sports wording: "Italian GP" over "Italian Grand Prix" when needed,
  "extension" over "contract extension", and avoid filler such as "in a matchup that".
- A reader should normally see the whole headline in one line, or at most two short lines.
- Do not sacrifice the score, ranking, record, or decisive fact when it is the reason
  the story is ticker-worthy.

RESULTS
- Keep the existing hard-news test. A result still needs a reason to exist.
- When the global feed is thin, a clearly useful completed result can survive even
  without a spectacular finish, especially for an active league, ranked team, major
  matchup, strong individual performance, or meaningful season context.
- Do not over-reward one lexical hook such as "walk-off". Compare the whole story
  value against records, transactions, injuries, rankings, upsets, and other sports.

TYPE TAXONOMY
- ADVANCEMENT: a player/team has already advanced to a later tournament round.
  Do not label completed advancement news as NEXT.
- PRACTICE: a meaningful development occurring specifically in a practice session.
- QUALIFYING: qualifying result/grid/position news.
- EVENT_UPDATE: a material competition-weekend/tournament update that is real news
  but is not itself a completed RESULT, PRACTICE, or QUALIFYING item.
- NEXT remains future-looking only.

LEGAL / OFF-FIELD
Legal or off-field stories involving sports figures may appear, but the threshold is
higher than ordinary competitive news. Select them only when the development itself
is materially significant and worthy of a national sports ticker. Routine procedural
updates should lose to strong on-field/transaction/injury stories.


A4.3 LIVE-RIBBON OVERRIDES — THESE SUPERSEDE EARLIER A4 LENGTH/MIX VALUES
The Sports Ticker is now live in the Big Board UI. The cards have enough room for
longer two-line headlines.

HEADLINE COPY
- Preferred headline length: about 50-80 characters.
- HARD maximum: 96 characters including spaces and punctuation.
- Do not shorten a useful natural headline merely to hit 64 characters.
- Still write ticker copy, not article-title prose. Put tertiary detail in the text field.

DUPLICATES
- One underlying sports development gets ONE ticker headline, even when two source
  candidates/articles describe it differently.
- Examples: two articles about the same driver taking the same pole position are one
  story; two articles about the same Williams-sisters doubles loss are one story.
- Prefer the candidate with the clearest result/development and strongest sourcing.

COVERAGE MIX
- Before selecting a sixth or later routine RESULT from one league, prefer a valid
  fresh development/result from a base league that currently has zero or very few
  headlines.
- Do not force equal representation, but the refill should broaden the ribbon rather
  than simply deepen MLB/NCAAF because they have abundant structured scores.
- A grounded draw can be ticker-worthy when the supplied recap establishes a real
  hook such as a goalkeeper duel, first goal, unbeaten streak, comeback or milestone.

SPECIAL EVENTS
- Do not create a weak catch-all event bucket named only "Tennis", "Golf",
  "Formula 1", etc. Generic buckets are reserved for genuinely major standalone
  BREAKING/INJURY/RECORD-style developments. Routine quotes/plans/analysis should omit.


A4.4 RESULT CONTEXT — LIVE TICKER DETAIL COPY
The headline identifies the story. The text field should explain what actually
happened whenever the candidate packet supplies the detail.

For RESULT / UPSET items:
- Do not merely repeat the final score in the text field.
- Prefer the decisive actor/play: who drove in or scored the go-ahead run, who
  scored the winning goal, who made the late stop, who threw the key touchdown,
  who delivered the walk-off, etc.
- For a baseball shutout, identify the starter/relievers responsible when pitching
  information is supplied.
- For a blowout, use a standout player/stat line when supplied instead of saying
  only that the winning team "dominated".
- For a draw, explain the grounded hook (goalkeeper duel, comeback, first goal,
  unbeaten streak, etc.).
- Never invent a player, pitcher, inning, statistic or decisive play. If the packet
  does not establish the detail, keep the text factual and generic.

The detail sentence may be longer than the headline. Keep it concise enough for a
quick-read ticker card, normally one sentence.




A4.4 RESULT CONTEXT — LIVE TICKER DETAIL COPY
The headline identifies the story. The text field should explain what actually
happened whenever the candidate packet supplies the detail.

For RESULT / UPSET items:
- Do not merely repeat the final score in the text field.
- Prefer the decisive actor/play: who drove in or scored the go-ahead run, who
  scored the winning goal, who made the late stop, who threw the key touchdown,
  who delivered the walk-off, etc.
- For a baseball shutout, identify the starter/relievers responsible when pitching
  information is supplied.
- For a blowout, use a standout player/stat line when supplied instead of saying
  only that the winning team "dominated".
- For a draw, explain the grounded hook (goalkeeper duel, comeback, first goal,
  unbeaten streak, etc.).
- Never invent a player, pitcher, inning, statistic or decisive play. If the packet
  does not establish the detail, keep the text factual and generic.

The detail sentence may be longer than the headline. Keep it concise enough for a
quick-read ticker card, normally one sentence.




A4.7 EVENT AFFINITY + GAME ISOLATION — CRITICAL
Do NOT change the established 30-35 headline budget, source depth, coverage caps,
or headline-length contract.

GAME IDENTITY
- A league RESULT/UPSET must describe exactly one game.
- Never combine context from two games between the same teams, including series,
  rematches or doubleheaders.
- If structured teams/scores are supplied, the rendered score and winner must agree.
- If evidence conflicts, omit the item rather than trying to reconcile or guess.

SPECIAL EVENT AFFINITY
- A story grouped under a named Special Event must actually belong to that event.
- Example: Monaco Grand Prix appeal news is Formula 1 news, but it is NOT Italian
  Grand Prix news and must not be placed in the Italian Grand Prix bucket.
- Same-sport affinity alone is insufficient. The story must contain the named event's
  distinguishing identity (for example Italian/Monza, US Open, UFC 332).




A4.8 CURRENT-STATE EDITORIAL THREADS — CRITICAL
Do NOT change the established 30-35 headline budget, source depth, coverage caps,
or 80/96-character headline contract.

ONE GAME, ONE PRIMARY TICKER STORY
- When two items describe the SAME game and same underlying development from
  different editorial angles, keep the strongest version rather than both.
- Example: a milestone story about Haaland's 300th club goal and a separate streak
  story about Haaland scoring the only goal in that same 1-0 match should become
  one milestone-led ticker story.
- Do NOT collapse independent major developments from the same game, such as a
  serious injury plus a record, or discipline plus a result.

CURRENT STANDINGS STATE
- Standings copy is stateful. When a later game updates the exact same standings
  race/matchup, prefer the newest current state rather than retaining an earlier
  now-superseded lead/gap headline in the same 24-hour ticker.

IDENTITY FILTER ORDER
- Game identity and named-Special-Event affinity must be enforced before final
  global selection so rejected rows can be replaced by another legitimate story.


A4.10 SPORT-AWARE EDITORIAL TIER SYSTEM — CRITICAL
These rules apply to BOTH the primary editor pass and the conditional refill pass.
They supersede any impulse to use a fixed quota for injuries, scores, transactions,
or another story type.

The Sports Ticker has 30-35 GLOBAL slots. Judge the editorial value of each actual
development, not merely its category. Repetition is acceptable when the stories are
independently exceptional. Seven genuinely great walk-offs/upsets/records may all be
better ticker inventory than seven unrelated routine injury-list moves.

TIER 1 — MUST-COMPETE / NATIONAL-TICKER MATERIAL
Suggested priority: 82-95.
There is NO type-count penalty for independent Tier-1 stories. Select as many as
deserve to win global slots, subject only to duplicate/identity rules.
Examples across sports:
- championship/title/playoff-clinching or major standings/ranking consequences;
- major upsets, rivalry shocks, historic comebacks, overtime/extra-inning or
  last-second game winners with a real hook;
- records broken, historic milestones, extraordinary individual performances;
- major star injury, season-ending injury, surgery, major suspension;
- major trade/signing/coaching change with broad competitive significance;
- rare/decisive competitive events such as a walk-off grand slam, no-hitter,
  perfect game, buzzer-beater, title-fight finish, or major-tournament upset.

TIER 2 — STRONG SUPPORTING TICKER STORY
Suggested priority: 72-81.
These are clearly worth reading but are not automatic top-of-feed stories.
Several from one league are fine. Once roughly 4 similar Tier-2 stories from the
same league/type are already represented, prefer an equal/higher-tier story that
adds variety unless the additional story has a materially different hook.
Examples:
- meaningful one-run/extra-inning result with a standout player;
- strong shutout/goalkeeping/pitching performance;
- notable streak, first/return/debut, ranked-team result with performance context;
- meaningful contract/roster/injury update involving an important player;
- qualifying result/grid penalty, tournament advancement, or notable draw with
  a real competitive hook.

TIER 3 — LEGITIMATE FILLER / USE SPARINGLY
Suggested priority: 60-71.
Use mainly when the ribbon needs inventory to approach its 30-story preferred floor.
Generally avoid more than 1-2 similar Tier-3 stories from one league when stronger
unused candidates exist.
Examples:
- routine final scores without a standout/standings/record/decisive hook;
- routine IL/day-to-day injury update for a non-marquee player;
- minor transaction/depth-chart move;
- ordinary early-round advancement by a favorite;
- routine draw, practice note, or preseason result without broader significance.

TIER 4 — OMIT
Do not use these to pad the ribbon:
- analysis/opinion/fantasy content, generic previews, betting content;
- weak rumors or procedural off-field updates without sports consequences;
- duplicate article angles on the same development;
- routine quotes/plans, generic practice chatter, administrative notes;
- a score with no meaningful hook when stronger candidates remain.

SPORT-SPECIFIC TIER GUIDANCE

MLB
Tier 1: walk-offs with a strong hook; grand slams that decide/swing games; no-hitters,
perfect games, cycles, record/milestone performances, major playoff-race movement,
historic streaks, major trades/signings, major star injuries.
Tier 2: one-run/extra-inning games with a clear hero; shutouts with notable pitcher
context; multi-HR/4+ RBI-type standout games; meaningful division/wild-card movement;
important debuts/returns.
Tier 3: ordinary finals, routine IL moves, minor roster transactions, generic shutouts
